summary: In 2026, fine-tuning sits at the end of a deliberate optimization sequence: exhaust prompt engineering first, then implement RAG when the model lacks domain knowledge, and only apply fine-tuning when behavior remains inconsistent at scale after both approaches have provably hit their limits. Fine-tuning bakes patterns, style, or task-specific skill into model weights, making it ideal for consistent tone, specialized behavior, or latency-sensitive deployments where large context windows are impractical. Most production systems layer all three techniques together, with fine-tuning reserved for cases where the cost and complexity are justified by measurable gains.
when_to_fine_tune: When prompt engineering and RAG have both been tried and the model still fails to produce consistent, reliable outputs at production scale.
When you need the model to internalize a specific style, tone, or domain behavior by default — not just when prompted carefully.
When inference latency or context-window costs make large system prompts or retrieval pipelines economically unsustainable.
When you have sufficient high-quality labeled or preference data (hundreds to thousands of examples) to justify the training cost and avoid overfitting.
